# Plugin Authoring

> **Read `internals.md` first** (plugins sit outside the rule chain, native `ngx` is available, shared memory dicts) and `rule-authoring.md` §6 (choosing between rules and plugins).
> The original official plugin API text is in `offline-docs/api.zh-CN.md`, section "Plugin".

---

## 1. Plugin Template (v4.1.0+, pre/post sub-phases)

### Standard header comment block (recommended)

```lua
---
--- <one-line description of what the plugin does>
--- Author: <signature>
--- Updated: YYYY/MM/DD
--- Changes: <summary of this change>
---
```

> Official built-in plugins (`plugin-ip-intelligence.lua`) use a four-line block of `--- Generated by UUSEC ... / --- Created by Safe3. / --- DateTime: ...`;
> **community and in-house plugins should use the version above** (description + author + update date + changelog), which carries more information and is easier to trace.

### Main body template

```lua
local _M = {
    version  = 0.1,          -- plugin version
    name     = "plugin-name",-- plugin name
    priority = 1             -- execution priority, higher runs first
}

-- <--- Configuration parameters --->
-- tunables are grouped up front, each annotated
local enableXXX   = true     -- master switch
local expireTime  = 7200     -- session lifetime (seconds)
local cookieName  = "SESSION" -- Cookie name

-- <--- Helper functions --->
local function helper(x) end

-- ssl phase (the waf argument is nil)
function _M.ssl_pre_filter(waf) end
function _M.ssl_post_filter(waf) end

-- request phase
function _M.req_pre_filter(waf) end
function _M.req_post_filter(waf) end

-- response header phase
function _M.resp_header_pre_filter(waf) end
function _M.resp_header_post_filter(waf) end

-- response body phase
function _M.resp_body_pre_filter(waf) end
function _M.resp_body_post_filter(waf) end

-- log phase
function _M.log_pre_filter(waf) end
function _M.log_post_filter(waf) end

return _M
```

- Phase functions with no work can be omitted.
- **Before v4.1.0** there were no sub-phases; the old function names were `req_filter` / `resp_header_filter` / `resp_body_filter` / `log`.
- **Meaning of pre / post**: they respectively mean **before / after** the WAF's own logic is processed.
- Each filter phase may return **two bools**: the first `true` = stop executing subsequent plugins; the second `true` = return directly, without executing subsequent **security rules**.

---

## 2. Execution Order and Position

```
Within the same phase:  plugin pre (by descending priority)  ->  security rule chain  ->  plugin post (by descending priority)
```

| Dimension | Conclusion |
|:---|:---|
| Ordering | By `_M.priority` in **descending** order; higher runs first |
| Relation to the rule chain | Sits **outside** the rule chain (pre/post straddle the rule chain); after a rule returns `RULE_ALLOW`, the **response header phase is skipped entirely** (including that phase's hooks), while the request / response body / log phases still run (see `internals.md` §3-3) |
| Short-circuit | Returning `return true, true` skips subsequent plugins and subsequent rules |
| Phases | ssl / req / resp_header / resp_body / log, each with pre + post |

> **This is the most fundamental difference between plugins and rules**: for mandatory validation that "cannot be bypassed by an allowlist" (authentication, auditing, rate limiting), use a plugin; for detection that "should be overridable by site policy", use a rule.

---

## 3. Available Objects

Inside plugins you can use **native `ngx`** directly (the plugin template itself depends on it):

```lua
local ngx        = ngx
local ngx_req    = ngx.req
local ngx_header = ngx.header
local ngx_exit   = ngx.exit
local ngx_time   = ngx.time
local ngx_kv     = ngx.shared        -- direct access to all shared memory dicts
```

| Native object | Purpose |
|:---|:---|
| `ngx.req.get_headers()` | Read request headers |
| `ngx.req.get_uri_args()` | Read query parameters |
| `ngx.req.read_body()` / `ngx.req.get_body_data()` | Read the request body |
| `ngx.header[...]` | Set response headers |
| `ngx.exit(status)` | Return directly (together with `return true, true`) |
| `ngx.shared.<dict>` | Shared memory read/write (**`db` has 32m, suitable for storing sessions**) |
| `ngx.time()` | Timestamp |

Optional third-party resty libraries: `resty.random` (secure random), `resty.string`, `resty.http`, etc.

**Choosing a shared dict**:

| Need | Choice |
|:---|:---|
| Sessions / tokens / mappings / key-values needing more space | `ngx.shared.db` (32m) |
| Access counters shared with the rule side | `ngx.shared.ipCache` (16m) |
| Manually incrementing block counters | `ngx.shared.ipBlock` (8m, note it is also read by built-in rule 13) |

> ⚠️ Rules **should not** depend on native `ngx` (`ngx.` appears 0 times across the 51 built-in rules); plugins **should** use it. See `internals.md` §6.

---

## 4. Authoring Conventions

| Convention | Description |
|:---|:---|
| **Required in the template** | `_M.version`, `_M.name`; `_M.priority` is required when multiple plugins coexist |
| **nil safety** | `(waf.host or "")`, `(waf.uri or "")` |
| **How to block** | Standard order: `waf.msg = "reason"` -> `waf.rule_id = <id>` -> `waf.deny = true` -> `ngx_kv.ipBlock:incr(waf.ip, 1, 0, 600)` -> `ngx_exit(403)` -> `return true, true` |
| **Second hit during a ban** | Use `waf.block(true)` to reset the TCP connection directly, reducing bandwidth consumption |
| **Sharing across phases** | `waf.ctx = <data>`, read in later phases |
| **Logging** | `require("waf.log")`; mind the noise and **encoding safety** (`log.utf8`) |
| **Response-phase variables** | `waf.status` exists only in the response header phase; `waf.respBody` exists only in the response body phase, and only when `respContentType` is text/html, text/plain, json, or xml |
| **Authentication response** | Use `ngx_exit(401)` + `WWW-Authenticate`, **do not return 200 to fake a normal response** |
| **Password comparison** | Use **constant-time comparison** to prevent timing attacks |
| **Example credentials** | The `users` in the official template are example values, **never copy them into production** |

### 🔴 Plugin-only variables (not present in rules)

The following three variables are **available only in plugins**; an actual measurement found 0 occurrences across the 51 built-in rules, while official plugins use them widely:

| Variable | Purpose |
|:---|:---|
| `waf.msg` | Log / alert message (fill in the "reason" when a plugin blocks) |
| `waf.rule_id` | Rule number written to the log (official plugins use plugin-specific ranges such as `10000` / `10001`) |
| `waf.deny` | Setting `true` means block |

**The standard way for a plugin to block** (from the original text of the official `plugins/ip-intelligence.lua`):

```lua
waf.msg     = "ip threat level: " .. level
waf.rule_id = 10000
waf.deny    = true
ngx_kv.ipBlock:incr(waf.ip, 1, 0)     -- plugins must increment the block counter manually
ngx_exit(403)
return true, true                      -- skip subsequent plugins and rules
```

> **The fundamental difference from a rule block**: a rule only needs `return waf.RULE_BLOCK, "reason"`, and the engine writes `ipBlock` automatically;
> a plugin must set `waf.msg` / `waf.rule_id` / `waf.deny` **itself**, call `ngx_exit(403)` **itself**, and increment `ipBlock` **itself**.

---

## 5. Plugin Logging API

```lua
local log = require("waf.log")

log.errLog(...)        -- write an error log to /uuwaf/logs/error.log
log.utf8(str)          -- convert character encoding to UTF-8, preventing errors when writing to the database/JSON
log.getReq()           -- get HTTP request information
log.encodeJson(obj)    -- Lua table -> JSON string
log.broker(func, ...)  -- proxy a function call with arguments
```

> Before writing to the database or JSON, **always** call `log.utf8` on non-ASCII text; otherwise an encoding error will cause the record to be lost.

---

## 6. Pattern Library

### 6.1 Auth plugin (Cookie session + auto renewal + ban on failure)

See `offline-docs/examples/plugin-auth-session.lua` (a complete community-contributed implementation). Core structure:

```lua
local _M = { version = 2.1, name = "auth-plugin" }
local ngx_kv = ngx.shared

-- site auth config {domain, username, password}
local site_auth_config = {
    {"app.example.com", "admin", "<set-a-strong-password>"}
}
-- path allowlist (any path containing these is allowed through)
local api_whitelist = { "app.example.com/v1/", "app.example.com/i/" }

local session_duration = 7200       -- session lifetime (seconds)
local cookie_name      = "WAF_AUTH_SESSION"
local session_prefix   = "sess:"
local max_login_attempts = 5
local renew_threshold  = 0.3        -- renew when remaining time falls below 30%

-- generate a random session ID
local function generate_session_id()
    local random_bytes = resty_random.bytes(32)
    if not random_bytes then
        ngx_log(ngx_ERR, "failed to generate random session ID")
        return nil
    end
    return resty_string.to_hex(random_bytes)
end
```

Key implementation points:

| Point | Approach |
|:---|:---|
| Session storage | `ngx_kv.db:set(session_key, expire_time, session_duration)` -- uses the **32m `db`** |
| Auto renewal | On read, check the remaining time; if below the threshold, refresh the expiry with `db:set` |
| Login failure counting | `ngx_kv.ipCache:get(login_attempts_key)`; after exceeding the limit, `ngx_kv.ipBlock:incr(waf.ip, 1, 0, 600)` |
| XSS prevention | HTML-escape user input before echoing it |
| Immune to IP drift | Use a **Cookie session** instead of binding to the IP |
| Path allowlist | Match by **path prefix containment** (note: this is a "wide allow"; allowing inside a plugin does not pass through the rule chain, at your own risk) |

> Key point: **do not hard-code sensitive credentials in the plugin**. A real deployment should read them from environment variables or a protected external configuration.

### 6.2 Basic auth (minimal implementation, official built-in `plugins/basic-auth.lua`)

```lua
local _M = { version = 0.1, name = "basic-auth", priority = 1 }

function _M.req_pre_filter(waf)
    local auth_header = ngx.req.get_headers()["Authorization"]
    if auth_header then
        local creds = decode_base64_authorization(auth_header)   -- implement it yourself
        if creds and authenticate(creds) then return false end    -- continue if it passes
    end
    ngx.header["WWW-Authenticate"] = 'Basic realm="Secure Area"'
    ngx_exit(ngx.HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED)      -- 401
    return true, true                    -- skip subsequent plugins and rules
end
```

### 6.3 Log shipping (official built-in `plugins/kafka-logger.lua`)

In the `log_pre_filter` / `log_post_filter` phases, push request logs to an external system (Kafka / HTTP / SIEM).

```lua
function _M.log_post_filter(waf)
    local log = require("waf.log")
    local payload = log.encodeJson({ host = waf.host, uri = waf.uri, ip = waf.ip })
    -- ship asynchronously via resty.http or broker
end
```

### 6.4 IP threat intelligence (official built-in `plugins/ip-intelligence.lua`)

In `req_pre_filter`, query IP intelligence (a local database or a remote API) and block on a hit:

```lua
function _M.req_pre_filter(waf)
    if is_malicious(waf.ip) then
        waf.msg     = "IP threat intelligence hit"
        waf.rule_id = <id>
        waf.deny    = true
        ngx_kv.ipBlock:incr(waf.ip, 1, 0)
        ngx_exit(403)
        return true, true
    end
end
```

### 6.5 Cookie renewal

| Parameter | Description |
|:---|:---|
| `cookie_duration = 0` | Session cookie (invalidated when the browser closes) |
| `cookie_duration > 0` | Persistent cookie (`Max-Age`) |
| `renew_threshold` | Renewal threshold (e.g. `0.3` = renew when less than 30% remains) |

- For persistent cookies, append a `Set-Cookie` renewal in `resp_header_post_filter`.
- Use **append mode**, do not overwrite an existing `Set-Cookie` header from the origin.

---

## 7. Plugin Output Convention

When the user asks you to write a plugin, output using the following structure:

1. **Requirements analysis** -> confirm why a plugin is necessary (can a rule replace it?)
2. **Solution summary** -> phase selection, data flow, execution order
3. **Threat model** -> attack types, key characteristics, bypass techniques
4. **Plugin code** -> ready to copy (header comment block + configuration parameters up front + sectioned skeleton)
5. **Test samples** -> should-block + should-allow + boundary (**including bypass attempts**)
6. **False positive analysis** -> scenarios that could be wrongly blocked
7. **Deployment advice** -> `priority`, canary rollout, log observation, rollback, performance impact
8. **Validation results** -> **the Lua syntax check output actually run**

### 🔴 Must be validated before delivery

| Check | Command | Pass criterion |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Lua syntax | On a WAF host: `wafcheck.sh lua <plugin file>` (authoritative) / elsewhere: `pcrecheck.py lua <plugin file>` (heuristic) | `SYNTAX_OK` / `BALANCED(heuristic)` |
| Every regex | `pcrecheck.py extract <plugin file>` (standalone version, PCRE2) / on a WAF host `wafcheck.sh file` may be used (same origin as PCRE1) | Exit code 0/1 (**2 = invalid regex**) |
| Dependencies exist | Check whether libraries such as `require("resty.http")` are available | No module not found |
| No hard-coded credentials | Manual review | Template example values must be replaced |
| **Semantic / hook check** | `rulecheck.py all <plugin file>` | No ❌ items (hook names, `_M` fields, APIs, `ngx` usage, modules) |
| **Module existence** | `rulecheck.py modules <plugin file>` | Every `require`d module is on the measured list (§10) |

> **Regex escaping reminder**: in a Lua short string `"\d"` is illegal (`invalid escape sequence`); it must be written `"\\d"`. In a `[[ ]]` long string it is kept as-is. For regex details see `rule-authoring.md` §2-2.

---

## 8. Common Pitfalls

| Pitfall | Description |
|:---|:---|
| **A plugin crash causes request errors** | When an HTTPS site errors out, first check whether it references a parameter that was not passed in (values such as `waf.scheme` that must be passed explicitly rather than being globally visible) |
| **Missing `priority`** | The outcome is undefined when multiple plugins coexist |
| **Treating a plugin as an "unbypassable last line of defense"** | Allowing skips subsequent rules and ML validation (the response header phase skips plugin hooks along with everything else) -> mandatory validation cannot rely on plugins alone: either do not write an allow rule, or add another layer outside the WAF |
| **Not transcoding before writing JSON / DB** | Non-ASCII text such as Chinese will encode incorrectly; use `log.utf8` |
| **Hard-coded credentials** | Example credentials from official templates must be replaced |
| **Returning 200 to fake successful authentication** | This breaks client behavior and downstream trust |
| **Making request-side decisions in the `respBody` phase** | The request context is already fixed in that phase; decisions belong in the request phase |
| **Blocking external calls on the request path** | Put slow operations such as shipping or DB lookups in the `log_*` phases, or proxy them asynchronously with `log.broker`; do not slow down every request |
| **Regex without `o`** | Use `"jo"` with `ngx.re` on request-path regexes to cache the compiled result, otherwise it is recompiled on every request |

---

## 9. Official Plugin Idioms (reusable)

Source: the three official plugins (`plugins/kafka-logger.lua`, `plugins/ip-intelligence.lua`, `plugins/basic-auth.lua`) + community `auth-plugin.lua` (offline copy named `offline-docs/examples/plugin-auth-session.lua`).

| Idiom | Approach | Why |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Store state in `ngx.shared.db`** | `ngx_kv.db:set(key, val, ttl)` | `db` is the largest dict (32m), suited to sessions/mappings |
| **The blocking quintet** | `waf.msg` -> `waf.rule_id` -> `waf.deny = true` -> `ngx_kv.ipBlock:incr(waf.ip,1,0,600)` -> `ngx_exit(403)` -> `return true, true` | A rule only needs to return a constant; a plugin must walk the whole set itself |
| **Auth failure should "look like" an auth failure** | `ngx_exit(401)` + `WWW-Authenticate` | Returning 200 as a disguise breaks the client and downstream trust chain |
| **Constant-time password comparison** | Do not return early during byte-by-byte comparison | Prevents timing side channels |
| **Second hit during a ban** | `waf.block(true)` cuts the connection directly | Saves bandwidth, lowers the attacker's cost-benefit |
| **Transcode before logging** | `log.utf8(str)` | Non-ASCII written to DB/JSON encodes incorrectly |
| **Immune to IP drift** | Bind the session to a cookie rather than an IP | IPs change on mobile networks; binding to IP would wrongly kill legitimate users |
| **Share between phases** | `waf.ctx = ...` | The standard means for a plugin to carry state across pre/post |
| **Example credentials must be replaced** | The `users` / `admin123` in official templates are placeholders only | Copying them into production = opening a backdoor |

---

## 10. Modules You Can require (measured on v7.2.5)

A plugin's `require` is constrained by nginx's `lua_package_path '/uuwaf/?.w;/uuwaf/?/init.w;;'`:
**the plugin's own `.w` files + the engine's embedded `waf.*` modules + the Lua module tree shipped with luajit**.

**Measured as available** (taken from `/uuwaf/luajit/share/lua/5.1/`):

| Group | Modules |
|:---|:---|
| Encoding / hashing / crypto | `cjson` `cjson.safe` `ngx.base64` `resty.md5` `resty.sha1` `resty.sha256` `resty.aes` `resty.rsa` `resty.zlib` |
| Network / protocols | `resty.http` `resty.http_connect` `resty.http_headers` `resty.dns.resolver` `resty.kafka.*` `resty.ldap.*` `net.url` |
| Storage / concurrency | `resty.lock` `resty.lrucache` `resty.mysql` + native `ngx.shared.<dict>` |
| Matching / acceleration | `resty.libinjection` `ahocorasick` `resty.radixtree` `resty.chash` `mmdb` |
| Other | `resty.random` `resty.string` `resty.htmlentities` `jsonschema` `tablepool` |
| **Engine-provided utility library** | **`waf.util`** (recommended; the official `ip-intelligence` plugin uses `require "waf.util"`) |
| **Other embedded engine modules** | `waf.dsl` (DSL rule evaluator), `waf.validator`, `waf.timer` (timers), `waf.url` -- the engine requires them itself; **their interfaces are undocumented**, so they are for awareness only and should not be relied on in delivered plugins |

**Measured as nonexistent** (using them raises an error immediately): `resty.redis`, `resty.memcached`, `resty.upload`, `resty.websocket.*`, `resty.session`, `resty.template`, `lfs`, `socket` (LuaSocket).

> ⚠️ The list changes between versions; **verify before moving across versions / instances**:
> ```bash
> docker exec <WAF container> sh -c 'ls /uuwaf/luajit/share/lua/5.1/resty/'
> docker exec <WAF container> sh -c 'find /uuwaf/luajit/lib -name "*.so"'
> ```
> Before delivery, compare automatically with `rulecheck.py modules <plugin file>` (the list is inlined in the script).
>
> Without Redis / LuaSocket: **use `ngx.shared.db` (32m) for caching** and **`resty.http` for outbound requests**; do not go looking for other libraries.

**`waf.util` already ships ready-made helpers, do not rewrite them yourself** (read out of the engine export table, v7.2.5):

| Category | Members |
|:---|:---|
| Strings | `split(str, sep)` `trim` `replace` `isSpace` `startWith` `endWith` `contains` `toLower` |
| Encoding | `urlDecode` `unescape_uri` `base64Decode` `decode_base64` `hexDecode` `hex2bin` `bin2hex` `htmlEntityDecode` |
| JSON | `jsonDecode` / `jsonEncode` (wrappers around `cjson.safe`, returning an error rather than throwing) |
| Matching | `rgxMatch` `rgxGmatch` `rgxSub` `rgxGsub` `regex` `pmMatch` `create_ac` `ac_match` (Aho-Corasick automaton) |
| Detection | `checkSQLI` `checkXSS` `checkRCE` `checkPT` `checkJson` `purify_sql` (wrappers around libinjection) |
| Other | `isIP` `getRootDomain` `inArray` `strCounter` `version` |
